parsed.explanation: An enforced sodomy statute (Article 135) with documented state torture during interrogation, confinement to mental hospitals, arrests of well-known figures, and vigilante violence in prisons — current through the 2022 criminal code, which increased severity and scope. Trans people are legally invisible, so a visitor whose documents or presentation expose birth-sex status falls directly into Article 135's scope if authorities read relationships as same-sex. There is no anti-discrimination law, no recourse, no civil society, and state media suppress independent reporting; the state is the perpetrator, not a bystander. This resembles the severe-risk anchors: sustained coercive targeting with failed remedy, though without documented execution policy. Thin data on enforcement frequency resolves toward the structural risk the enforced statute, torture record and zero-recourse framework imply. A trans visitor discovered here faces imprisonment, torture and custody abuse — severe, current, state-directed exposure.
